query: When should adults be vaccinated against diphtheria in Ontario (Canada)?
llm-response:
In **Ontario, Canada**, adults should be vaccinated against diphtheria as part of their routine immunization schedule. The diphtheria vaccine is given in combination with tetanus (and sometimes pertussis) as **Td (tetanus-diphtheria)** or **Tdap (tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis)**.

**Recommended schedule for adults:**

- **Booster every 10 years:** Adults should receive a **Td (tetanus-diphtheria) booster every 10 years**.
- **One-time Tdap dose:** Adults who have not previously received a dose of Tdap (which includes protection against pertussis/whooping cough) should get a **one-time Tdap booster**, replacing one Td dose.

**Special situations:**
- **Pregnancy:** All pregnant women should receive a Tdap dose in every pregnancy, ideally between 27–32 weeks gestation.
- **Wound management:** If an adult has a wound and their last Td/Tdap dose was more than 5 years ago, a booster may be recommended.

**References:**
- [Ontario Ministry of Health – Routine Immunization Schedule](https://www.health.gov.on.ca/en/pro/programs/immunization/schedule.aspx)
- [Canadian Immunization Guide – Diphtheria](https://www.canada.ca/en/public-health/services/publications/healthy-living/canadian-immunization-guide-part-4-vaccine-preventable-diseases/page-6-diphtheria.html)

**Summary:**  
Adults in Ontario should get a Td booster every 10 years, and a one-time Tdap if not previously received. This protects against diphtheria, tetanus, and (in the case of Tdap) pertussis.

query: When should adults be vaccinated against pneumococcal disease in Ontario (Canada)?
llm-response:
In **Ontario, Canada**, pneumococcal vaccination recommendations for adults depend on age, health status, and risk factors. Here’s a summary based on current guidelines (as of 2024):

---

### **1. Adults 65 Years and Older**
- **All adults aged 65+** are recommended to receive **one dose of pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (Pneu-P-23, Pneumovax®23)**.
- This is publicly funded (free) in Ontario.

---

### **2. Adults 18–64 Years with High-Risk Conditions**
Adults with certain medical conditions are at higher risk and should be vaccinated **regardless of age**. These include:
- Immunocompromising conditions (e.g., HIV, organ transplant, cancer, asplenia/splenic dysfunction)
- Chronic kidney disease (including those on dialysis)
- Chronic heart, lung, or liver disease
- Diabetes mellitus
- Cochlear implants
- Cerebrospinal fluid leaks

**Recommended vaccines:**
- **Pneu-P-23 (Pneumovax®23):** One dose, publicly funded for high-risk groups.
- **Pneu-C-13 (Prevnar®13):** May be recommended in addition to Pneu-P-23 for certain high-risk groups (e.g., immunocompromised, asplenia). This is **not publicly funded** for adults in Ontario, but may be covered for some specific conditions.

**Timing:** If both vaccines are recommended, Pneu-C-13 should be given first, followed by Pneu-P-23 at least 8 weeks later.

---

### **3. Revaccination**
- Some high-risk adults may require a **second dose of Pneu-P-23** at least 5 years after the first dose (e.g., those with immunocompromising conditions or asplenia).

---

### **4. Healthy Adults 18–64 Years**
- **Routine pneumococcal vaccination is not recommended** for healthy adults under 65 unless they have specific risk factors.

---

### **Summary Table**

| Group                        | Vaccine(s) Recommended | Publicly Funded? |
|------------------------------|-----------------------|------------------|
| Adults ≥65                   | Pneu-P-23             | Yes              |
| High-risk adults 18–64       | Pneu-P-23 (+/- Pneu-C-13) | Yes (Pneu-P-23) |
| Healthy adults 18–64         | None                  | N/A              |

---

**References:**
- [Ontario Ministry of Health: Pneumococcal Vaccine Information](https://www.health.gov.on.ca/en/pro/programs/publichealth/flu/docs/pneumococcal_factsheet.pdf)
- [Public Health Ontario: Immunization Schedules](https://www.publichealthontario.ca/en/health-topics/immunization/vaccine-preventable-diseases/pneumococcal)
- [Canadian Immunization Guide: Pneumococcal Vaccine](https://www.canada.ca/en/public-health/services/publications/healthy-living/canadian-immunization-guide-part-4-vaccine-preventable-diseases/page-16-pneumococcal-vaccine.html)

---

**If you have a specific medical condition or are unsure about your eligibility, consult your healthcare provider or local public health unit.**
